title: Communicate the country totals
prompt: Return each billing country and total invoice value, highest total first.
hint: Group by BillingCountry. Sum invoice totals directly so invoice-line joins do not duplicate revenue.
answer:
Reference SQLite query:
SELECT BillingCountry, SUM(Total) AS revenue FROM Invoice GROUP BY BillingCountry ORDER BY revenue DESC, BillingCountry
checks: I used the requested population and filters.
I checked the unit of analysis and missing values.
I can explain the result and any ties.
sql: SELECT BillingCountry, SUM(Total) AS revenue FROM Invoice GROUP BY BillingCountry ORDER BY revenue DESC, BillingCountry

title: Join without losing meaning
prompt: Return the five tracks with the most units sold, showing track name and units. Break ties by TrackId ascending.
hint: Join InvoiceLine to Track on TrackId. Sum Quantity; use a deterministic tie break.
answer:
Reference SQLite query:
SELECT t.Name, SUM(il.Quantity) AS units FROM InvoiceLine il JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId=il.TrackId GROUP BY t.TrackId, t.Name ORDER BY units DESC, t.TrackId ASC LIMIT 5
checks: I used the requested population and filters.
I checked the unit of analysis and missing values.
I can explain the result and any ties.
sql: SELECT t.Name, SUM(il.Quantity) AS units FROM InvoiceLine il JOIN Track t ON t.TrackId=il.TrackId GROUP BY t.TrackId, t.Name ORDER BY units DESC, t.TrackId ASC LIMIT 5

title: Prevent a duplicated total
prompt: Using the ETL case discussion of joins and aggregation, explain why joining invoice totals to invoice-line records and summing those totals can overstate sales. Describe a repeatable fix.
hint: What happens to a single invoice total when an invoice has three lines?
answer: A header total repeats for every matching line. Aggregate lines to invoice level before joining, or sum the header table separately. Reconcile row counts, distinct invoice identifiers and control totals. Do not use SUM(DISTINCT total): different invoices can share the same value.
checks: I identified the grain of each table.
I explained the duplication mechanism.
I described a reconciliation and a repeatable fix.

title: Explain the payroll change

hint: Divide total wages by total hours; do not average individual hourly rates.

Investigate employees behind the three largest eligible changes before recommending action.

title: Interpret an effect
prompt: Using the restaurant case, investigate whether temperature and game days are associated with sales. Explain how the interaction of prior-year sales and a game day changes the interpretation.
hint: An interaction changes the slope associated with another predictor.
answer: Fit and document the relevant models. For an interaction model, Sales = b0 + b1×PriorYearSales + b2×GameDay + b3×PriorYearSales×GameDay. The prior-year slope is b1 on non-game days and b1+b3 on game days; game-day difference is b2+b3×PriorYearSales. Interpret estimates and uncertainty from your fitted output. An association alone does not establish causation.
checks: I specified the predictors and interaction.
I interpreted coefficients conditionally.
I discussed statistical uncertainty and causality.
source: Restaurant · temperature, game day and interaction tasks

title: Turn a policy into a test

title: Investigate split purchases
prompt: Design a test for possible split purchases around the $5,000 limit. Explain your grouping choices, possible false positives and next audit steps.
hint: Related transactions may use different cardholders, vendors or dates. A single grouping cannot catch every case.
answer: Start with same-cardholder, same-vendor, same-day purchases below or equal to $5,000 whose combined amount exceeds $5,000. Restrict the agency and period, separate refunds and inspect dates. Review invoices and purchase purpose to establish whether a known purchase was split to evade a limit. Discuss missed splits across days, vendors or cardholders and unrelated legitimate purchases flagged by the rule.
checks: I specified the grouping and thresholds.
I considered refunds and alternative splitting patterns.
I requested corroborating evidence.
